pos.personaBrief: No verified possession evidence (gap axis); from general knowledge Sacchi wanted to dominate the game in both phases, consistent with the verified 'fluid, highly organised attacking 4-4-2' and high pressing, so he rejects ceding the ball by design.

pro.personaBrief: Gap axis, answered from general knowledge: Sacchi's Milan attacked vertically and quickly after high regains (verified high pressing and 25-metre compactness), with Van Basten runs in behind, rather than patient short build-up under pressure.

est.personaBrief: The verified 'highly organised' 4-4-2 with zonal marking and a fixed 25-metre block points to a positional, rehearsed structure where each player knows his zone, while the 'fluid' attack allowed forwards and wide midfielders to move inside.

lar.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: the verified 4-4-2 used wide midfielders and overlapping full-backs rather than touchline wingers, with Gullit and Van Basten as central decisive players.

blo.personaBrief: Verified facts: a high defensive line with no more than 25 metres between defence and attack, high pressing and the offside trap, so the block is high and forwards defend first.

mar.personaBrief: Verified: 'Sacchi's teams adopted a zonal marking system', the defining feature of his Milan; defenders protect spaces and no star gets a man-marker.

pla.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: Sacchi imposed his game model on Milan and Italy and played the same pressing, high-line football whoever the opponent, consistent with the verified organised 4-4-2.

res.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: Sacchi held that winning must come with merit and beauty and that great teams are remembered for how they played, though with Italy he was somewhat more pragmatic.

sis.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: Sacchi is the archetype of system over talent, demanding everyone press and defend (verified high pressing and compactness require all eleven) and believing the collective elevates ordinary players.

jog.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: his high-pressing, compact system demanded great physical intensity and running from every player, and he notoriously sidelined low-running playmakers such as Baggio with Italy, while still valuing intelligent passers in midfield.

bas.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: Milan combined academy players like Maldini and Costacurta (starting young) with big signings like Gullit, Van Basten and Rijkaard; Sacchi chose on fit to the system rather than age or origin, focused on winning.

lid.personaBrief: Gap axis, from general knowledge: Sacchi was an obsessive, demanding authority figure who drilled players relentlessly and applied the same rules to stars, decisions being his alone.
